thinking_text:
**Evaluating functional intentions**

I'm considering how to weaken the functional intention of a tool by increasing its strength and resistance to bending. Adding more material could help reduce stress around the throat area. I want to avoid overstating the stress level, so I need a reasonable inference to mark confidence. I should copy the complete request sentence, and I wonder if "REQ-001" could be a unique request ID. I’m also checking for action words and specific validation features.

request.raw_text: If this is a spanner, the main cutout is too deep which is weakening the tool. Make the cutout shallower by 10mm, but keep the "size" of the spanner the same - meaning the parallel surfaces remain 20mm apart.
action_words: keep the "size" of the spanner the same
functional_intention_words: the main cutout is too deep which is weakening the tool
keep the "size" of the spanner the same

aim.primary_aim: Reduce the depth of the spanner's main cutout by 10 mm to avoid weakening the tool while retaining a 20 mm separation between its parallel sizing surfaces.

functional_design_intentions.name: Reduce tool weakening
functional_design_intentions.description: Retain more material at the main cutout by making it 10 mm shallower, with the intention of reducing the cutout's weakening effect on the tool.

functional_design_intentions.name: Preserve spanner size
functional_design_intentions.description: Maintain the spanner size defined by the two parallel surfaces remaining 20 mm apart.

required_relationships.reference: the two surfaces defining the spanner size
the two parallel surfaces must remain 20 mm apart

targets_to_preserve.reference_geometry: the two parallel surfaces defining the spanner size
targets_to_preserve.preservation_rule: Preserve their parallel relationship and their 20 mm separation while changing the cutout depth.

targets_to_preserve.reference_geometry: all geometry not required to reduce the main cutout depth
targets_to_preserve.preservation_rule: Apply a minimum-change constraint and preserve non-targeted geometry.

geometry.description: The spanner's main cutout is 10 mm shallower than its initial state, while its two parallel sizing surfaces remain 20 mm apart.

relationships.reference: the two surfaces defining the spanner size
the two parallel surfaces remain 20 mm apart

functions.name: Maintain spanner size
functions.description: The final spanner retains the size defined by a 20 mm opening between the parallel surfaces.

functions.name: Reduce cutout-induced weakening
functions.description: The shallower main cutout retains more tool material and reduces the weakening attributed to excessive cutout depth.

behaviors.name: Improved structural resistance
behaviors.description: The additional retained material at the shallower cutout is intended to improve resistance to structural weakening under tool loads.

validation_criteria.description: The final main cutout depth is reduced by exactly 10 mm relative to its initial depth.
The two surfaces defining the spanner size are parallel.
The perpendicular separation between the two parallel sizing surfaces remains 20 mm.
The final geometry retains the stated 20 mm spanner size while reducing the excessive cutout depth.
The shallower cutout retains more material in the affected region, reducing the cutout's stated weakening effect.
Non-targeted geometry remains unchanged except where necessarily affected by the shallower cutout.

unresolved_requirements.description: The exact model feature corresponding to the "main cutout" is not identified by an explicit feature or section ID.
candidate_interpretations: The main cutout is the primary open-ended jaw recess bounded by the two parallel 20 mm sizing surfaces.
The main cutout is another dominant recess in the tool.

candidate_interpretations: Depth is the inward extent of the main cutout from its opening toward its deepest boundary.
